body:
## Symptom

On the self-hosting pdca-pdca instance, the T3 repo-scoped suite gate goes red **exactly and only** on stacked bundles (a `stack-base` marker present). The retained gate log for pdca-pdca's issue_457 names the failure precisely: 11 failures, all `test_verify_base.VerifyBaseExport`, all of the shape

```
AssertionError: 'origin/pdca-integration/main' != 'UNSET'
```

The only two stacked bundles in that instance's 37-cycle corpus (issue_419, issue_457) are precisely the ones with this T3 red signature. The reviewer on issue_457 confirmed the failures reproduce only when `PDCA_VERIFY_BASE` is present in the ambient environment.

This is very likely also (part of) the recurring "unclassifiable T3 driver-suite red" that instance chased across 2026-08-05/06 Act reviews — unreproducible at sign-off because a hand rerun has no `PDCA_VERIFY_BASE` exported.

## Mechanism — two layers

1. **The driver exports the verify base to every gate, not just the bundle-scoped verifier.** `template/src/pdca_harness/gates.py` (the block resolving `PDCA_BASE` / `PDCA_VERIFY_BASE`, currently around line 379–397) adds `PDCA_VERIFY_BASE=origin/<stack-base>` to the env of **all** configured gate rows for a stacked bundle — including repo-scoped rows like the T3 suite and T2 docs check. The variable is only meaningful to the C4 per-fix verifier (the base it must reset to before applying `patch.diff`); to a repo-scoped suite it is contamination.

2. **`test_verify_base` is not hermetic against ambient bases.** `template/tests/test_verify_base.py`'s `VerifyBaseExport.setUp` never masks ambient `PDCA_BASE` / `PDCA_VERIFY_BASE` / `PDCA_BRIEF_BASE`, and `gates.run_gates` merges the ambient environment into the gate subprocess (`_merged_env`). So when the suite itself runs *inside* a driver gate for a stacked bundle, every test's gate command inherits the outer export and the `UNSET` assertions fail.

Either layer alone would have prevented the observed red; fixing only (2) still leaves repo-scoped gates of any instance running with a bundle-scoped base in their environment.

## Suggested fix

- Scope the `PDCA_BASE` / `PDCA_VERIFY_BASE` export to the bundle-scoped verify gate (the row that consumes it), or provide a way for repo-scoped rows to opt out.
- Independently, make `VerifyBaseExport` (and any other env-sensitive suite) mask the three base variables in `setUp`, so a self-hosting target's T3 run is deterministic regardless of the caller's environment.

## Evidence

- pdca-pdca `results/issue_457/gate-logs/T3-suite.log` — `FAILED (failures=11, skipped=2)`, all in `VerifyBaseExport`; root/template suite green in the same run.
- pdca-pdca `results/issue_457/SUMMARY.md` §5 — reviewer reproduction: failures occur only with `PDCA_VERIFY_BASE` leaked.
- Correlation: stacked bundles 419/457 red; the non-stacked cycles of the same waves green (453, 456, 468).

Found at the pdca-pdca Act review of 2026-08-09 (process/act-log.md).
title: gates: the stacked-bundle verify-base export leaks into repo-scoped gates — env-sensitive target suites go red on every stacked bundle
